Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement

Questions to Ask Before Any Non-Surgical Breast Treatment, and Red Flags

Use this checklist at a consultation. A trustworthy provider welcomes questions.

Home/Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement/Non-Surgical Breast Enhancement/Questions to Ask Before Any Non-Surgical Breast Treatment, and Red Flags

Use this checklist at a consultation. A trustworthy provider welcomes questions. This page is part of our guide to non-surgical breast enhancement.

About the treatment

  • What exactly is it intended to do for the breast?
  • What is the evidence for breast use, and where is it published?
  • How long do results last, and how is that known?
  • What are the risks, and how are complications treated?
  • What are the alternatives, including doing nothing?

About the product

  • What is the product name, manufacturer and batch number?
  • Is it approved or registered for this use?
  • Is it absorbable? If so, what happens as it dissolves?

About the clinician

  • What are your registration and specialist qualifications?
  • How many of these treatments have you done in the breast?
  • Who treats complications, and where?

About the setting

  • Is this a licensed medical facility?
  • What emergency arrangements exist?
  • How do I contact you out of hours?

About costs and consent

  • What is included in the price, and what is not?
  • Will I get written information and time to decide?

Red flags

  • Guaranteed results or cup-size promises
  • Pressure to book or pay quickly, or time-limited discounts
  • Reluctance to name the product
  • Before-and-after photos that cannot be verified
  • No medical history taken
  • Treatment offered outside a medical setting
  • Claims that it is "risk-free", "natural" or "permanent"

Take your time

You can leave, think and get another opinion. Read breast enlargement safety for warning signs and complaint routes.

Key takeaway

If you cannot get clear answers, walk away.
